decision: Qualification completed with findings; retain harness/evidence, no runtime change. Ordinary recall omits 5000 older eligible memories and E11-F1 remains open.

earlier_smoke_attempts.outcome: Harness sent duplicate repository_id to project-scoped command URL; server rejected before any note mutation. Request corrected.

All 50 context calls executed, but exact restoration-packet assertion failed because of E11-F1. Final harness preserves and reports freshness differences, compares every other restored field and still compares unchanged reads in full.

findings.impact: The restored note is served with current dependency hashes and coverage.stale_memories=0, but freshness.stale_count remains 625. Changed-source notes were correctly withheld; this is a diagnostic consistency finding.
findings.summary: Source-byte restoration restores note eligibility but leaves memory stale markers in the repository freshness ledger.

limitations: Synthetic authored decisions over 40 tiny Python files. Isolates memory catalogue size, not simultaneous large source/graph size or independent real-user relevance. Ordinary recall is limited to the newest 20000 eligible memories; older-note retrieval is recorded rather than assumed. No observer/model authoring, cross-repository permissions or concurrent writers are measured.
Restoration differs in freshness only; all other packet fields match. No claim that event-driven stale markers automatically reconcile after reversion.

Authoring completed through 25000 public API calls, but authoring throughput and peak memory were not measured. Setup server stopped before retrieval; no builds, tests, other fixture preparation or benchmarks overlapped timed calls.
The displayed time ranges are ranges of per-probe medians; each uses three samples after one warmup. These are feature costs, not controlled performance improvements.
method: All notes authored with the public note API and original file dependencies. Setup HTTP server stopped before fresh CLI/measurement-worker retrievals. One excluded warmup per workload/probe, alternating workload order, complete repeated packet equality, exact source and note contents, token budgets and source-change/restoration checks.
